evidence: The agent quotes stats_pb.d.ts as proto2 with `required double jitter = 3` and `required double current_round_trip_time = 13`, plus a captured toJson() payload that still carries zero doubles, so the field cannot vanish at 0.0. But reply 2, posted 30s after the pushback, said 'Plan: valid finding, different fix' and proposed a null-carrying parse. Reply 4 retracted that. The final outcome (no guard, plus a zeros test) is right, but the thread argued both sides.
guidance_note: Settle the premise against the schema before posting a plan, and post one plan per thread: here a templated 'valid, different fix' reply contradicted the evidence-backed pushback already posted on the same thread.

evidence: `selected_candidate_pair_changes` is `required uint32` in a proto2 schema. Twelve measured runs printed real counts and never 'undefined pair changes', so the reviewer's 'most healthy runs' prediction is refuted. Reply 2 nonetheless pasted the same 'valid finding, different fix' null-parse plan, and reply 4 retracted it.
guidance_note: Don't paste one templated plan across sibling threads; the pair-changes thread already had run evidence that contradicted the plan.

evidence: Deployed runs printed `level 0.00e+0`, so a 0.0 audioLevel is present and `.toExponential` runs on it, and the field is `required double audio_level = 41` under proto2. Reply 1 pushed back correctly. Reply 2 then claimed 'Confirmed ... undefined is representable' from the TS `?` typing, which reply 1 had just explained away. Reply 4 retracted.
guidance_note: Treat the protobuf-es TS `?` as typing noise and check the generated runtime (proto2 required) before agreeing a field can be undefined.

evidence: Run against the old parser, the regression test fails with `actual: ['10.0.0.2','10.0.0.2']`, which proves the per-connection `T01` ids collide in one Map. The reviewer asked only for a test. The agent parsed each array separately in `ofOne()`, which makes the collision unrepresentable.
guidance_note: Before writing 'nothing below depends on which connection an entry came from', check whether any lookup keys on ids scoped to that source; here the id resolution depended on it.

evidence: Every `stats()` fixture emitted only an audio inboundRtp entry, so the `kind === "audio"` filter was asserted by nothing. 9eb1388 adds a video entry and asserts it is excluded.
guidance_note: Every filter needs a fixture containing an element it must exclude.

evidence: `delivered()` awaited the native `getRtcStats()` unbounded inside the try whose finally deletes the room, while join and subscribe both use `rejectAfter`. 9eb1388 wraps it in `Promise.race` with `rejectAfter(10_000, ...)` inside Caller, matching the existing convention.
guidance_note: When adding a new await on a native or network call, apply the module's existing bounded-wait convention (`rejectAfter`) at the same time.

evidence: The agent's grep confirms that dtlsState, bytesReceived and silentConcealedSamples appear only in fixtures, and jitterMs only at zero. The mutation table then shows each mutation passing before d792728 and failing after it. The gap predates review; F5's fix added coverage for one unasserted output and did not sweep the other returned fields.
guidance_note: When a reviewer flags one unasserted output field, enumerate every field the function returns and assert each with a distinguishing nonzero value in the same fix.

evidence: 9eb1388, the F4 fix, wrote the `ofOne` doc 'Its output holds no ids a caller could cross-reference', but the transport object it returns still carries `id: entry.rtc.id`. The agent dropped the dead field (no readers anywhere) and narrowed the comment.
guidance_note: When writing an invariant comment such as 'output holds no ids', check it line by line against the return statement it describes before pushing.

evidence: `relayProtocol` had no reader and no assertion, and `remote.type`, which pathLine prints, was unasserted; both claims are true. `remote.protocol` does not exist on `endpoint()`'s return, so that part was wrong. The agent dropped relayProtocol, asserted remote.type, and pushed back on remote.protocol. F7's coverage sweep in d792728 had stopped short of the `endpoint()` fields.
guidance_note: When sweeping a return shape for unasserted fields, include the nested objects (here `endpoint()`'s fields), not only the top-level ones.

evidence: pathLine never printed dtlsState, and the diff hunk shows the pathLine body from the original PR. d792728 only added a test comment explaining why dtlsState matters, which made the pre-existing omission visible, so the flag is a false positive. 8608573 prints `dtls ${transport.dtlsState}` unconditionally.
guidance_note: When a parser computes a field for a diagnostic purpose, check that the renderer actually prints it before claiming the diagnostic exists.

evidence: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md each carry a parallel 'Why: an image built from a working tree...' paragraph (visible in #12's hunk headers), so a second prose copy that can diverge is real. The agent deferred it to ticket openconv-docs-e9q after the PR had merged. 8608573 does not touch either doc, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: When adding the same policy to AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, give it one owner and make the other file a pointer from the start.

evidence: account/rtpLines/pathLine/rtpLine are module-private in a script that logs at import time, and the agent itself conceded on F10 that pathLine has no test. The formatters date from round 0; 8608573 only appended a dtls term to pathLine, so the flag is a false positive. Deferred to ticket openconv-acceptance-x6f.
guidance_note: Put branching report formatters in an importable module from the first commit so they can be tested next to the parser they render.

evidence: The code really does build an all-undefined endpoint when `candidates.get` misses, which is inconsistent with the `pair ? ... : null` refusal. Whether rtc-node ever emits a pair that references an absent candidate is not shown in the packet; the reviewer says so too. The agent filed openconv-stats-61f with establishing reachability as its first task. The candidate lookup is unchanged since round 0, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: When a parser refuses incomplete data at one level (no transport, no pair), apply the same decision to every lookup inside that level when first writing it.

evidence: AGENTS.md says 'then file that tag into the homelab's service-versions.auto.tfvars.json', while CLAUDE.md says 'let the update-service-version action file the tag' (both visible in #12's hunk context), so the two docs disagree on who writes the file. Deferred to openconv-docs-e9q. 8608573 does not touch the docs, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: When writing a short summary of a longer doc, copy the mechanism verbatim or leave it out; don't paraphrase who performs a step.

narrative: This PR adds an RTC-stats parser. Round 0 had three wrong-premise findings (proto3 field absence on proto2 required fields). The agent pushed back with schema evidence, then posted contradictory 'valid, different fix' plans on the same threads and retracted them hours later. Round 1 consisted entirely of fix-caused findings: the F4 restructure left a false 'no ids' comment, and F5's coverage fix didn't sweep the other unasserted fields, which recurred again in round 2 for `endpoint()`. The PR merged at 02:47 with four round-3 findings untriaged; they were answered and ticketed at 03:15, after merge.
guidance_observations: Two plan comments 30 seconds apart on each of F1-F3 took opposite positions on the premise, which suggests a templated plan was posted across sibling threads without reading each one.
Merging before replying to the final round's findings left them resolved by tooling and untriaged; the agent had to backfill tickets after the fact.
Coverage findings arrived one field-group per round (filter, then four fields, then endpoint fields); one enumeration of the returned shape would have closed them in round 0.

evidence: The Dockerfile header says 'Published by CI from a commit it fetched itself' while no CI publish existed yet; #12's 510ef3a later rewrote the same header to 'To be built in CI ... No job builds it yet', confirming the overclaim. The PR was closed as 'unneeded' with no reply, so whether a response was owed depends on that abandonment.
guidance_note: Write docs for a planned replacement in future tense until the replacement exists in the repo.

evidence: The hunk shows the script comment starting 'Three behaviours below are worth carrying over, and openconv-deploy-690.3 names them', but the heredoc and the CLAUDE.md lines the reviewer says repeat the list are not in the packet. The PR was closed unreplied as 'unneeded'.
This duplicates F1 on the same line: the present-tense 'Published by CI' claim when no publish path existed. The PR was closed unreplied.
guidance_note: Write docs for a planned replacement in future tense until the replacement exists in the repo.

narrative: This PR is a docs-and-disable change to the working-tree build script. One round raised three comment findings: two duplicates about the Dockerfile overclaiming CI publishing, and one duplication concern. The agent did not reply and closed the PR as 'unneeded'.
guidance_observations: The present-tense overclaim about CI recurred in #12 (F6) in AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, so the lesson from this unreplied finding was not carried forward.

evidence: The agent confirmed act_runner `capacity: 4`, so concurrent jobs share one daemon and the fixed `openconv-buildkit-probe` tag could collide. 7d4df6c adds a run-scoped tag and a concurrency group, both of the reviewer's options.
guidance_note: On a shared multi-capacity runner, scope every named Docker artifact by run id when first writing it.

evidence: `${location#http://$REGISTRY}` is a no-op for any other scheme or host and builds `http://...5000https://...`. The reviewer suggested a distinct error for a foreign host; the agent instead stripped any scheme and authority with sed, and verified all three spellings normalise.
guidance_note: When normalising an external header value, test every form the spec allows (absolute, relative, foreign host) before pushing.

evidence: The agent showed the registered runner row `["ubuntu-latest","ubuntu-24.04","ubuntu-22.04"]` for homelab-runner. The file lives in `.gitea/workflows/`, which GitHub never reads, and a sibling repo uses the same label against the same registry.

The probe hard-coded `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7` and the cache mount separately from the Dockerfile. The agent derived the syntax line from `head -n 1` and added a mount-kind extractor, going beyond the suggestion. That extractor and its hand-written `covered=" cache "` ledger produced F5, F11 and F18 in later rounds.
guidance_note: When writing an extractor that claims to find 'every' X, write the accept/reject table first (key order, implicit defaults, which side is a hand-kept ledger) and test it.

evidence: The F4 fix used `grep -o -- '--mount=type=[a-z]*'`, which misses `--mount=id=foo,type=secret`. The agent conceded 'it lands squarely on the claim I made last round', and 510ef3a now selects --mount tokens first, verified against three key orders. b43c218 is a docs commit; the cause is 7d4df6c.
guidance_note: Before claiming an extractor finds every key=value option, test it with the key in first, middle and last positions.

evidence: b43c218 added AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md text saying a push 'triggers a build' and naming ci-builder.yaml, but that workflow only builds a throwaway busybox probe. b43c218 was new doc content, not a fix for any finding, so there is no cause to name.
guidance_note: Describe what the workflow in this PR does today, not what the epic will make it do; the same overclaim was already flagged in #10.

evidence: Cleanup ran after `docker build` under `set -e`, so a failed build leaked the mktemp dir. 510ef3a installs an EXIT trap right after mktemp. The build-then-rm sequence dates from 5dfdf42; the F1 fix only renamed the tag, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: Under `set -e`, install an EXIT trap immediately after acquiring any resource rather than writing cleanup after the step that is designed to fail.

evidence: This is the same leak as F7. The reviewer's suggested trap used `docker image rm "$tag" 2>/dev/null || true`. The agent's trap reports a missing image on stderr instead of silencing it. The leak is pre-existing, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: Under `set -e`, install an EXIT trap immediately after acquiring any resource.

evidence: The POST-then-DELETE upload probe in 5dfdf42 cancels only if every intervening step succeeds, so an abort orphans the session. 510ef3a moves the cancel into an EXIT trap. That trap was installed after the emptiness check, which produced F12. The leak predates review, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: Install the cleanup trap immediately after the call that acquires the resource, before any validation of its result.

evidence: AGENTS.md said 'See CLAUDE.md for the full rule' after restating it in four paragraphs, and the F6 fix had to correct the same sentence in both files. The duplication was introduced by b43c218's unprompted doc addition, not by a fix. 2bc26e5 cut AGENTS.md to a pointer, but added a new copied phrase (F17).
guidance_note: When adding a policy to AGENTS.md that CLAUDE.md owns, write only the pointer plus the bare rule.

evidence: The F4 fix (7d4df6c) introduced a hand-written `covered=" cache "` ledger, and its error text invited extending the ledger rather than the probe. The agent conceded 'Deriving the kinds from the Dockerfile only closed half the loop'. 2bc26e5 derives `covered` from the generated probe using the same extractor.
guidance_note: When fixing a one-source-of-truth finding, check that the fix itself introduces no new hand-written copy, including the coverage list on the checking side.

evidence: 510ef3a, the F9 fix, installed `trap cleanup_upload EXIT` after `if [ -z "$location" ]; then exit 1`, so an opened but unparseable session never got cancelled. That contradicts the new comment 'The trap cancels on every exit path'. 2bc26e5 moved the trap above the check.
guidance_note: When adding a cleanup trap, place it on the line right after resource acquisition and check every exit between acquisition and the trap.

evidence: `awk '/^[Ll]ocation:/'` is case-sensitive beyond the first letter, while the sibling check uses `grep -qi`. HTTP header names are case-insensitive. The awk pattern is in the round-0 hunk (5dfdf42) and 2bc26e5 did not change it, so the flag is a false positive. Fixed in 2a4fba3 with `tolower($1) == "location:"`.
guidance_note: Match HTTP header names case-insensitively everywhere, the same way the sibling check in the same file already does.

evidence: 2bc26e5 moved the trap above the emptiness check without guarding it, so an empty `path` now fires `DELETE http://$REGISTRY` and prints a blank session note; before the move that path exited without any DELETE. The agent added an early return with a note instead of the suggested `|| true`, which would have swallowed real cancel failures.
guidance_note: When moving a trap ahead of validation, walk the trap body through each state it now newly covers (here an empty path).

evidence: `run: |` is a YAML literal block scalar whose common indentation is stripped before bash sees it, so `PROBE` and `SHELL` arrive flush-left. Run 4828 on 2bc26e5 printed `buildkit-ok` from inside the generated Dockerfile, which could not happen if the heredoc never terminated.

510ef3a, the F6 fix, added to CLAUDE.md 'checkout matches the triggering commit, runner is x86_64 with a BuildKit-capable Docker daemon, registry reads and writes', a restatement of ci-builder.yaml's own header. 1e9e8a3 replaced it with a pointer. The 2a4fba3 flag is incidental: that commit touched only the workflow.
guidance_note: When correcting a doc's overclaim, state the policy-level fact and point at the owning file rather than enumerating its current behaviour.

evidence: 2bc26e5, the F10 dedup fix, added to AGENTS.md the verbatim CLAUDE.md phrase "I'll just build it on gpu this once", a new copy introduced by a fix meant to remove copies. The reviewer also wanted the bare gpu rule collapsed to one site. The agent removed the quote and kept the one-line rule at each entry point, a defensible split.
guidance_note: A fix that cuts duplication must not add text copied from the owning file; reread the new lines against the owner before pushing.

evidence: The F5 fix's extractor (`grep -oE 'type=[a-z]+'` per token) yields nothing for a `--mount` with no `type=`, which BuildKit treats as bind, so neither side would ever ask about it. 1e9e8a3 maps a token with no type to `bind`, and the agent caught a BSD-sed `t;` portability bug in its own first attempt.
guidance_note: When fixing an extractor's key-position gap, also enumerate the key-absent case and its implicit default in the same pass.

narrative: This PR adds a Gitea CI reachability probe and build-policy docs, and reached the 5-round review cap. The mount-kind guard added for F4 was reopened three times: key order (F5), the hand-kept covered ledger (F11), and implicit bind (F18). The upload-session trap fix (F9) was installed after validation (F12); moving it ahead then fired a bogus DELETE on an empty path (F14). Doc fixes kept re-creating duplication: the F6 correction enumerated the workflow's checks (F16), and the F10 dedup copied CLAUDE.md's phrase into AGENTS.md (F17). Round 4 consisted entirely of fix-caused findings.
guidance_observations: Each fix to the mount-kind guard was verified only against the case the reviewer named; one accept/reject table at F4 time would have closed F5, F11 and F18 together.
Several round-1 threads stayed unanswered until the round-2 push ('left open by my process slip'), so plans were not posted before fixes landed.
Both pushbacks (F3 runner labels, F15 YAML heredoc) were settled with direct evidence (runner table row, green run output) rather than argument, which is the right shape.

evidence: The new Dockerfile header says the workflow builds it 'for master and for a manual dispatch, and publishes the result as YYYY.MM.DD.N and' :latest, which restates publish-image.yaml's `if:` and tag steps. 0f751b7 cut it to a pointer naming the owner.
guidance_note: When updating a pointer comment to name a new owner, name the owner without restating what it owns; #12 had already drawn the same finding on docs.

evidence: The agent reproduced the bug under bash: `08` gives 'value too great for base', and `010` gives tag .9 instead of .11. Its first check had run in zsh and missed this. 0f751b7 applies `10#${highest:-0}` and reruns the resolver suite with padded cases.
guidance_note: Verify shell snippets under the interpreter that will run them (bash, not zsh), and force base 10 on any externally sourced digit string before arithmetic.

evidence: This duplicates F1 on the adjacent line: the Dockerfile restates the publish condition and the YYYY.MM.DD.N/:latest scheme owned by publish-image.yaml. The same 0f751b7 edit closed both.
guidance_note: When updating a pointer comment to name a new owner, name the owner without restating what it owns.

narrative: This PR adds the real publish workflow. Round 0 raised two real findings: a Dockerfile comment restating the workflow's gating and tag facts (reported twice) and bash octal arithmetic on a registry-sourced tag counter. Both were fixed in one commit, and round 1 approved with no findings.
guidance_observations: The agent's first verification ran in zsh rather than bash and wrongly cleared the octal bug; matching the verification interpreter to the runtime would have caught it before review.
The Dockerfile restatement repeats a pattern flagged several times in #12, so that lesson did not carry over to the next PR.
